page_text:
Edit CSV files online, as a table and as text

The CSV Editor shows the raw CSV and the table side by side. Edit a cell in the table and the editor changes exactly that field in the text - the other quotes, the separator and the line endings stay as they were. A click in the table shows the field in the text, and the cursor in the text shows its cell. That makes it quick to fix exports from shops, banks and databases, clean up address lists, or prepare data for import.

Everything runs in your browser. Your files are kept there, not on our server, and there is no sign-up and no advertising.

What the editor can do

Like a spreadsheet

Type into cells, move with the arrow keys and Tab, copy and paste ranges from and to Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets, add, delete and move rows and columns.

Any CSV

Comma, semicolon, tab or pipe as separator, detected by itself; with or without a header row; UTF-8 with or without BOM and Windows-1252; Windows and Unix line endings are kept.

Find what is broken

Rows with a different number of fields, quotes that are never closed, empty and repeated column names - listed with their line, one click away.

Sort, filter, look closer

Sort and filter the view without touching the file, or sort the data itself. The column panel shows the kind of values, empty and different ones, sum and average.

Big files

The table only draws the rows you see: files with 100 000 rows stay quick to scroll, filter and edit.

Export

Excel workbook (XLSX), JSON, Markdown and HTML tables, TSV, or CSV with another separator and encoding - with protection against spreadsheet formulas.

How it works

  1. Open - drop a CSV file into the window, open it with "Open file…", or start with a template under "New".
  2. Edit - change cells in the table or the text on the left; both follow each other. Use "Insert" for rows and columns, "Format" for the separator.
  3. Save - download the CSV as it is, or export it as XLSX, JSON, Markdown or HTML.

Use the editor on your own website

Put the editor into your own website with an iframe or in a window of its own. Your page hands it the document, gets every change and every save back, and can let an AI send its results to your server. No sign-up, no key.

Embed the editor on your website →

Frequently asked questions

Is my CSV file uploaded?

No. The editor runs in your browser and keeps your files there, not on our server. A file goes to a server only if you set up a webhook to your own server, if a website that embeds the editor saves it on its own server, or if another website opens it here with a form (post.php) - our server then passes it straight to your browser without storing it. As on any website, the server logs each visit, and we count page views anonymously - see the privacy policy.

Does the editor change my file when I edit one cell?

Only that cell. The editor writes the change into the CSV text exactly where the field is and leaves the rest as it was: the other quotes, the separator and the line endings stay. A field is put in quotes only when it needs them.

My CSV uses semicolons - does that work?

Yes. The editor detects comma, semicolon, tab and pipe as separator; you can also choose it under Format. Convert turns the file into another separator.

How do I open the CSV in Excel without broken umlauts?

Export it as XLSX, or download the CSV with a byte order mark (BOM) - select the checkbox under Format or choose "UTF-8 with BOM" in the export. Excel then reads UTF-8 correctly.

Can it handle large files?

Yes. The table only draws the rows you see, so files with 100 000 rows stay quick to scroll, filter and edit.

Where are my documents saved?

Only in your browser. Click the folder button at the top left (My documents) to open, rename, duplicate, download or delete them. Clearing your browser's site data removes them, so download the ones you want to keep - or let the editor send them to your own server ("Save to server"). Very large files may not fit into the browser's storage; the editor tells you when that happens.

Can an AI write in the CSV Editor?

Yes, any AI - ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or the AI in your coding tool. Click "AI Assistant", then "Copy prompt", paste it into your AI and say what it should do. The AI answers with a link; click it and the table appears in your editor. "Undo" takes every change back.

No. The editor is free, without ads and without sign-up.

embed.h1: Embed the CSV Editor in your website
embed.intro: For developers: how to put the CSV Editor into your own page - in an iframe, in a window of its own or as a read-only viewer - and how documents, saves and AI results travel between the editor and your server. You need no sign-up and no key from us.
embed.body:
Any https page (and localhost) can embed the editor with an <iframe> and ?embed=1 - no sign-up, no key. Embedded, the editor hides the page text and shows a Save button. There are four ways to get the table in and out.

1. Open a file from a link, save to your server

src= opens a file (your server must allow CORS), webhook= makes "Save" (Ctrl+S) send the document to that address. Add &auto to save after every change.

<iframe src="https://csv.giit.ch/?embed=1&src=https://your-site.com/data/products.csv&webhook=https://your-site.com/save.php"
        allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>

The webhook gets a POST with JSON { editor: "csv", event: "save", id, name, content, updated }. A link carries no token (it would end up in server logs and the browser history), so a webhook in the address suits a save address that needs none, for example on localhost or in your intranet. For a public server, hand the webhook over with a token in csveditor:load (hook: { url, token }) and check it, as this small PHP script does:

<?php
header('Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://csv.giit.ch');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization');
header('Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, OPTIONS');
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'OPTIONS') exit;
if (($_SERVER['HTTP_AUTHORIZATION'] ?? '') !== 'Bearer SECRET') { http_response_code(403); exit; }
$d = json_decode(file_get_contents('php://input'), true);
$name = preg_replace('/[^\w\- ]/u', '_', $d['name']);
file_put_contents(__DIR__ . "/data/$name.csv", $d['content']);
echo '{"ok":true}';

The data directory beside save.php must already exist and be writable by PHP.

2. Your page holds the document (postMessage)

The editor says csveditor:ready, your page answers with csveditor:load, the editor reports csveditor:loaded, csveditor:change on real edits and csveditor:save when the user saves. Your page may send csveditor:get (the current state) or csveditor:save (press Save). Saving then goes through your own login and session.

<iframe id="ed" src="https://csv.giit.ch/?embed=1" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
<script>
const ed = document.getElementById('ed');
const ORIGIN = 'https://csv.giit.ch';

addEventListener('message', async e => {
  if (e.source !== ed.contentWindow || e.origin !== ORIGIN) return;
  const m = e.data;
  if (m.type === 'csveditor:ready') {               // the editor is ready: hand it the document
    ed.contentWindow.postMessage({
      type: 'csveditor:load',
      name: 'Products',
      content: await (await fetch('/data/products.csv')).text()
    }, ORIGIN);
  }
  if (m.type === 'csveditor:change') document.title = '● not saved';   // a real edit
  if (m.type === 'csveditor:save') {                // the user clicked "Save"
    await fetch('/api/save', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ name: m.name, content: m.content }) });
    document.title = 'Saved';
  }
});

// A save button on your own page: the answer comes as csveditor:save
function saveNow() { ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'csveditor:get' }, ORIGIN); }
</script>

AI Assistant inside your page: it works in the frame too. With allow="clipboard-write" on the iframe, "Copy prompt" uses the clipboard directly (otherwise the editor falls back to the old copy command, or shows the prompt to copy by hand). A link the AI sends cannot reach an editor inside another website, so the editor tells the AI and the user to paste the AI's whole answer into the editor instead - or open the editor in a window of its own.

3. In a window of its own

window.open("https://csv.giit.ch/?embed=window", "csveditor-17") opens the full editor in its own window and speaks the same messages with window.opener. Links from an AI reach it there. csveditor:load may also carry context: { host, title, rules } - the AI prompt then says where the document belongs and follows your rules - and hook: { url, token }, a webhook for this document only that is never stored. Closing the window with unsaved changes sends csveditor:closing.

4. AI through your own server

Hand the editor your own prompt, an address on your site and a key for this editor session. The AI dialog then shows "Connected to" your site, what you tell the AI, and the choice change the current document or make a new one; Copy prompt puts it all together. The AI posts its result with the key to your server, and your page opens it in the editor - a new document opens separately and stays in the user's browser. One key per editor session: it stays valid while the editor is open, and only while it has none the editor asks for it with csveditor:key-request. The editor never sends the key itself and never stores it; the address must be https on your own host or a subdomain of it.

const key = async () => (await fetch('/api/ai-key.php?doc=17')).json();   // one key per editor session
const k = await key();
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'csveditor:load', name: 'Products', content, ai: {
  label: 'My Site', prompt: 'Keep the column names. Prices in CHF.',
  endpoint: 'https://your-site.com/api/ai-result.php', key: k.key } }, ORIGIN);
// remember the id from csveditor:loaded and ignore change/save/closing with another id
// only while the editor has no key:
if (m.type === 'csveditor:key-request') { const k = await key(); ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'csveditor:ai', key: k.key }, ORIGIN); }
// while the editor is open, tell your server every minute; closing the editor or the page voids the key
setInterval(() => fetch('/api/ai-key.php?alive=' + k.key.slice(0, 8)), 60000);
// your server has a result (polling, SSE …): target is "current" or "new"
ed.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'csveditor:load', name: 'Products', content: draft, from: 'ai', target }, ORIGIN);

Make keys with at least 128 random bits, store only their hash, bind each to the logged-in user, the document and this editor session, make one per session, keep it valid only while your page reports the session as open, and void it when the editor or the page closes.

Your own AI dialog and answering instructions: with dialog: "page" in ai, a click on AI Assistant sends csveditor:ai-click with a request id; answer { type: "csveditor:ai-click", request, handled: true } within 300 ms and show your own dialog - otherwise the editor opens its own. answer: "…" puts your text in place of the "HOW TO ANSWER" part of the copied prompt ("none" leaves the part out, "" brings the editor's part back); the prompt then carries no key. When your server gives no key, answer csveditor:key-request with { type: "csveditor:ai", decline: true, message: "…" }: the editor stops waiting at once and shows your message after your host - write it in your page's language. In the prompt the document always stands in a fence longer than any run of backticks in it, marked as data.

The whole protocol is in llms.txt - give it to an AI and it builds the connection for your system. The other giit editors work the same way with their own prefix - editors.giit.ch.

Show a document read-only (viewer)

?viewer=1 shows only the finished document: no code, no tools, nothing can be changed, and nothing is stored in the browser. The document comes from a link (#b64=, ?src=), from your page with csveditor:load, or by POST as a normal form to post.php: the field content as text or b64 as base64, optionally name, at most 20 MB of text.

<form method="post" action="https://csv.giit.ch/post.php?viewer=1" target="_blank">
  <input type="hidden" name="name" value="Report">
  <input type="hidden" name="b64" value="…">
  <button>Open</button>
</form>

Without viewer=1 the document opens in the normal editor. Either way it is kept in memory only: it is not stored on the server and does not join "My documents". Opened directly, the viewer says that the content comes from a third party.

Templates with placeholders

When your server fills placeholders into the CSV before it is used, add template=mustache for {{name}}, {{#name}} … {{/name}} and {{^name}} … {{/name}}, or template=angle for <<name>> and <<?name>> … <</?name>>. The list of problems reads every tag as one placeholder and reports a section left open, a stray end tag, an end tag in the wrong order and a tag with an unknown sign; the code shows the tags as written. A tag is a cell value or part of one. A row of section tags only is a control row: the checks pass over it, and sorting and removing repeated rows keep every block between control rows in its place.

Send your placeholders with examples, and the table shows the rows filled with them: sections by their example state, a list once per example row, control rows left out. An example is a cell value as it is, with any separators, quotes and line breaks in it. A placeholder without an example shows its label in brackets, such as [Name]. The switch Template in the table’s bar shows the template’s table with the tags, Examples brings the examples back; the box Placeholders below the code puts a tag at the cursor. A cell that shows an example cannot be changed in the table; a click on it leads to its tag in the code. Examples are shown as text, stay in memory only and never reach your page: saving, change, get, the webhook and every export carry the template as written.

frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'csveditor:template',
  placeholders: [
    { name: 'name', kind: 'value', label: 'Name', example: 'John Doe' },
    { name: 'street', kind: 'value', label: 'Street', example: '1 Main Street' },
    { name: 'hasNote', kind: 'section', label: 'With a note', shown: true },
    { name: 'items', kind: 'list', label: 'Items',
      fields: [ { name: 'item', label: 'Item' }, { name: 'quantity', label: 'Quantity' } ],
      rows: [ { item: 'Chair', quantity: '2' }, { item: 'Table', quantity: '1' } ] } ] }, ORIGIN);
// or the same object as the field template of csveditor:load; { type: 'csveditor:template', clear: true } ends it
<iframe src="https://csv.giit.ch/?embed=1&template=mustache" allow="clipboard-write" style="width:100%;height:800px;border:0"></iframe>
